question: Does a 30 W chip stay under 85 C with a 10 CFM, 20 Pa fan blowing along the fins in a 40 C cabinet?
headline: With 232 L/min of air through its duct, the faces shed heat at 29.8 W/(m2 K) on average, and 30 W brings the hottest point to 77 C against a limit of 85 C.
confidence_reasons: grid convergence failed: pressure drop 3.539 -> 3.868 -> 4.045 Pa over 3 grids, grid convergence index 32% (observed order 2, extrapolated 4.473 Pa), so the grid is too coarse for this answer
residuals: largest final residual 0.0032 (k), every field fell at least 1.4 orders, close to converged, so the key number may still move slightly

wall resolution: y+ on the walls averages 6.53, at most 11.3, for wall functions, so part of the wall sits in the buffer layer, where wall functions are least accurate, though the blended wall function keeps the error to a few percent
operating point: the curve gives 3.58 Pa at 232 L/min, and the fine grid needs 4.05 Pa there (13% apart), so the coarse grid's fit set the flow a little off
hand calculation: heat balance on a uniform skin gives 69.2 C; the FEA skin averages 72.6 C (12% of the rise). Biot 0.00013: the part is nearly isothermal
convective heat transfer from RANS is commonly within 10 to 25% of measurements
